title: Nocturne Observer — Handoff & Quick Procedures (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, noisy scratchpad for the night shift (Nocturne Observer). Not polished — intended as a fast handoff and a set of short-lived mitigations to be replaced by proper runbook pages when time allows. Keep lightweight: what I needed to know at 02:00 and what I want the next person to pick up.

Quick TL;DR (first 5 minutes)
- Systems to glance at: inference-prod (latency), gateway-auth (4xx spike), cache-layer (KV miss rate).
- If token latency climbs > 250ms p50 or error rate > 0.8% for 10m, start escalation checklist.
- Recent incidents: kernel-fallback on g4-pool (2026-03-09) — watch for repeat fallbacks.

What I saw at shift start (2026-03-10 22:45 PST):
- infra-alert: gateway-auth 4xx burst cleared after restart of auth-proxy (see incident note below).
- embedding-QPS normal but 95th latency drifting up ~30ms from baseline.
- cache-layer KV miss rate at 7% (higher than typical 1–2%) — likely stale prefix caching due to rollout.

Immediate actions I performed
- Rotated auth-proxy pod (kube rollout restart deploy/auth-proxy -n infra). Confirmed 4xx tail cleared in ~90s.
- Increased cache warmup worker concurrency temporarily: /ops/scripts/cache_warmup.sh --concurrency=6 (reverted at 23:30).
- Added a short-lived routing rule to route non-SLA traffic to cheaper-variant model to relieve g4-pool (console: routing -> manual -> route id quick-relief-0310).

Current open risks / watch items (priority order)
1) KV miss uptick: check for recent model rollouts that bumped prefix patterns (product deployed embedding-v2 2026-03-10 21:12).
   - Quick check: /ops/tools/kv-stats --since 2026-03-10T20:00 | grep miss_rate (expect <2%).
2) Kernel fallback noise: if we see >3 kernel-fallback events in 30m across g4-pool, escalate to infra (pager: Ethan).
3) Billing-surge guard: routing change for quick-relief-0310 increases spend on dedicated pool — watch cost dashboard for >10% deviation.

Short procedures (step-by-step)
- Auth 4xx burst
  1. Check /infra/alerts -> alert gateway-auth-4xx.
  2. kubectl get pods -n infra | grep auth-proxy. Find pod with high restart_count.
  3. kubectl logs pod/<pod> -n infra | tail -n 200 for 4xx cause.
  4. If logs look transient, do a graceful restart: kube rollout restart deploy/auth-proxy -n infra.
  5. If restart not clearing, flip routing: console -> services/auth -> fallback to legacy-auth until infra team investigates.
  6. File quick incident note: channel #oncall-notes -> post summary and link to confluence draft.

- Cache warmup spike (temporary):
  - If miss_rate > 5% and client tail latency > 150ms, run cache_warmup with limited concurrency: /ops/scripts/cache_warmup.sh --prefix=recent --concurrency=6 --limit=50k
  - Monitor kv-stats and token-latency for 15m. If no improvement, revert concurrency to 2 and open ticket (JIRA-OPS-4182).

- Temporary routing rollback (how I did quick-relief-0310)
  - Console -> Routing -> Create manual route, scope: non-sla.*, traffic split 30% -> embedding-lt, 70% -> embedding-main.
  - If this introduces downstream 5xx, immediately revert route to 100% embedding-main.

Escalation contacts (order matters)
- First: Ethan Gomez (pager) — infra kernel/runtime issues, g4-pool.
- Second: Laura Chen (slack) — cache and routing config owner.
- Third: SRE lead (oncall-lead@redwood.ai) — for production-impacting incidents.

Incident note (kernel-fallback 2026-03-09):
- Event: qemu kernel fallback on g4-pool during a heavy transcription workload. Triggered when sequence length spikes + quantized kernel mismatch.
- Temporary mitigation taken: rotated to fallback-optimized model variant and increased batching cap.
- Follow-up: infra to check kernel matrix and add model->kernel compatibility tag.

Open TODOs I couldn't finish
- Formalize prefix list that triggered cache thrash (file updated local: /home/priya/tmp/prefixes-20260310.txt).
- Add a dedicated alert for KV miss rate > 3% sustained 15m (raised but not onboarded).
- Write short playbook for manual routing rollback in Console (confluence: TODO page).

Notes to next person (short and actionable)
- First 10m: glance dashboards, then check /ops/tools/kv-stats for miss_rate and /ops/tools/latency-overview for token latency.
- If you touch routing: always annotate the route with reason and expected duration. We had a silent routing change last week that confused the CS team.
- If you escalate to Ethan: include last 30m of kernel-fallback logs (awslogs group: /redwood/g4/kernels).

Things I would like to see in a proper runbook (future work)
- Clear threshold configs for when to degrade routing, with cost delta estimate.
- Automatic cache warmup job that runs post-rollout for models with new prefix patterns.
- A troubleshooting checklist for kernel fallbacks (diag steps, logs to copy, relevant metrics).

Random scratch/commands (notes to self)
- Check kernel fallback counts: /ops/diag/kernel_fallback_count --window=30m --pool=g4-pool
- Tail recent auth logs: awslogs tail /redwood/auth --start="1h" | grep 4xx
- Revert route: console -> routing -> quick-relief-0310 -> revert (or curl api: POST /api/v1/routing/revert?id=quick-relief-0310)

Unresolved questions
- Why did embedding-v2 change prefix behavior? was it the tokenizer patch or the quantization step? Need dev contact.
- Does the cache warmup worker respect TTL properly under heavy churn? observed potential leak at ~23:10.

Sign-off checklist before handing off to AM shift
- [ ] Clear any manual routes OR annotate with owner + ETA
- [ ] Post short handoff summary to #oncall-notes (1–3 bullets)
- [ ] Create follow-up ticket for anything left in TODOs

Handoff summary (to paste into Slack):
Nocturne Observer — Priya K (22:45–23:30)
- Resolved gateway-auth 4xx burst with auth-proxy restart.
- Temporarily routed non-SLA traffic to embedding-lt to relieve g4-pool; watch cost.
- KV miss rate elevated (7%) — likely tied to embedding-v2 rollout. TODO: formal prefix list + alert.

— end of scratchpad —

(If you find this useful, I'll tidy and move to shared runbooks. If not, it's a messy brain dump that saves 5–10 minutes next shift.)
